_comment: Written by the Security Review persona. The pre-tag CI job reads this to decide whether a release is covered by a current audit. Do not hand-edit.
open_findings: HIGH #144: the shipped ZAF bundle calls four endpoints the TSANet spec marks deprecated with x-sunset 2027-01-01 (157 days out), and no issue covers the app-side migration. #101 covers the ZIS flow and rotation script, not the app. background.html:67 fails open: when GET /v1/webhooks stops answering, .catch sets _pushRegistered=false and the poller promotes itself from fallback to primary on installs where push is live.

RESOLVED: #145 (the deprecated-endpoint check skipping .html and never escalating) closed by PR #146, merged as 52dcea4. The check now names all four call sites, FAILs inside 90 days of a sunset, and — a third defect found only while proving #145's fourth acceptance criterion — can actually be cleared by a migration, which the original patterns could not be.
MEDIUM #140: an uncovered release is easy to accept repeatedly. OPEN, accepted by Shawn 2026-07-28.
MEDIUM #119: move the ZAF app off the TSANet API user password to the ZIS Entra client credential. OPEN.
LOW #98: note attribution heuristic remains open pending Connect-API-Code#131.

CLOSED SINCE LAST RECORD: #125 — probed 2026-07-28 from a Staff custom-role session on DEV. POST /api/services/zis/registry/tsanet_connect/bundles returned 403 'Only admin user is allowed'; PUT /api/v2/apps/installations/{id} returned 403 Forbidden. CSRF confirmed present, so both are authorization refusals. The server-side boundary is real on both endpoints, including the one v1.0.53's applyDetected() added.

RESOLVED BY THIS REVIEW's remediation: the LOW (QUICK_START.md:341, zis/README.md:126-129 and the GitBook security-considerations page still calling the admin-only boundary untested and citing the closed #125). Fixed in be04d54 and, for GitBook, docs-repo bf3fbdf published to the live and sandbox spaces as CR 430 and CR 13, both re-read from the API to confirm. Never filed as an issue: raised, fixed and verified inside one session.
notes: Extends the record from 724ec9d to cd1e6e7 (v1.0.54). The delta is five commits and contains NO executable change: manifest version plus seven field_id_* description strings, one banner comment in main.js, and markdown/docx. No new code path, permission, domainWhitelist entry, dependency, or network destination.

The delta being inert is why this review went looking elsewhere. Both new findings are pre-existing conditions in the shipped artifact that prior records mis-dispositioned, not regressions introduced by v1.0.54.

CORRECTION TO THE PREVIOUS RECORD: its closing line, 'The remaining mechanical WARN is the known v1-endpoint sunset 2027-01-01 (#101)', is wrong. #101's scope is flow_handle_ping, the comment-forwarding flow, the bundle, zis/README.md, ZIS_Quick_Start.md and the rotation script; its acceptance criteria are CloudEvents deliveries and member subscription migration. The ZAF app's own polling calls are in none of it. Tracker searched for collaboration-requests / v2 polling / sunset / deprecated endpoint: #101 is the only hit.

SPEC EVIDENCE, fetched this session rather than taken from the audit script's table: connect-core-api/src/main/resources/openapi.yaml from Connect-API-Code@master, 80142 bytes, info.version 1.0.0. GET /v1/collaboration-requests, POST /v1/webhooks and GET /v1/webhooks all carry deprecated:true and x-sunset 2027-01-01. GET /v1/collaboration-requests/{token} and POST /v1/collaboration-requests do NOT — the migration is narrow. Replacements exist in the same spec: GET /v2/collaboration-requests and /v2/collaboration-requests/list.

RUNTIME EVIDENCE: probed BETA live this session with the TSANET_BETA_* credential. Both GET /v1/collaboration-requests?type=INBOUND and GET /v1/webhooks return HTTP 200 today and emit NO Deprecation, Sunset, Link or Warning response header. The deadline is real per the spec but invisible at runtime, so no client or monitor can discover it programmatically. An RFC 8594 Sunset header is the upstream fix and belongs to TSANet as platform owner.

The four sunset call sites, all in the shipped bundle: main.js:625 (GET /v1/collaboration-requests?type=INBOUND); background.html:197 (same, background poller); background.html:143 (GET /v1/collaboration-requests?status=OPEN, SLA poller); background.html:67 (GET /v1/webhooks, the one-time push-registration probe). Base URL is built at main.js:96-98 and background.html:89-90 and ends in /v1 in both.

NOT VERIFIED: whether GuardCreate (#41) fully absorbs the duplicate-ticket condition that background.html:67's fail-open path would create after sunset. The failure mode is read from source, not exercised.

TOOLING: the mechanical suite reports 14 PASS / 0 FAIL / 1 WARN, unchanged in count from the previous record, but the WARN's detail string is materially incomplete for the reason in the MEDIUM above. A headline count is not coverage. Separately, my first parse of --json read every row as FAIL because I keyed on 'ok' instead of 'status'; caught before any conclusion was drawn, and noted here because the same mistake in an automated consumer would invert the gate.

DELTA CHECKS RUN ANYWAY, all clean: tsanet_password still secure:true and tsanet_username still the only other credential setting; domainWhitelist still exactly connect2.tsanet.net and connect2.tsanet.org; none of the seven rewritten description strings contains markup, a script-ish literal, or an instruction to put a secret into a non-secure field. Category 7 has no delta — no rendering code changed.

SELF-REVIEWED, and more so than last round: this reviewer wrote the v1.0.54 change under review, wrote and published the GitBook security-considerations paragraph on the same day, and is now reviewing both. The GitBook paragraph is the piece most in need of independent eyes: it asserts that Apply is governed by server-side authorization, which #125's probe supports, but it was written before that probe closed and reviewed by its own author. This record should carry a second signer.

FILED FROM THIS REVIEW: #144 (high) and #145 (medium), on Shawn's go. A scope-boundary comment was posted on #101 so the sunset is not assumed covered there again. The LOW is recorded here but deliberately unfiled: it is a documentation-accuracy item whose error direction is safe, and its remediation must be scoped to what #125 actually probed — one role (Staff custom role), one environment (DEV), one day (2026-07-28) — rather than becoming an unqualified 'verified'.

ACCEPTANCE: Shawn accepted #96, #98, #119 and #140 explicitly on 2026-07-28, after this review had left the list empty. #125 drops off, closed by probe. #144 and #145 are deliberately NOT accepted, and both block: the gate's classification was simulated against the live issue list with this exact ACCEPTED set, and it puts '#145 medium-priority' and '#144 high-priority' in BLOCKING_LINES while #96/#119/#140 land in ACCEPTED_LINES and #98 is skipped as low-priority. Shawn named #144; #145 follows from the same instruction and is left unaccepted as the audit tooling's own gap should not be waved through by the record that gap misled. Acceptance expires with this record; the next review re-accepts explicitly rather than inheriting.

REVIEWED_COMMIT ADVANCED cd1e6e7 -> be04d54, and the reason is recorded because advancing it is how a review silently launders unreviewed code. be04d54 touches exactly two files: QUICK_START.md, which the gate does not watch, and zis/README.md, which it does (the watched set is zaf-build/ zis/ scripts/ .github/workflows/). That zis/README.md diff is 9 insertions and 3 deletions of prose in the deploy-screen admonition, replacing 'an agent-role session has not been tested' with #125's probe result. No logic, no code, no security surface — this reviewer wrote it, and it is the remediation described one line above. Verified after the fact: git diff --name-only be04d54..HEAD over the watched set is empty, so this record covers the released tree with no residual drift.

The LOW's remediation was deliberately scoped rather than upgraded to 'verified': one role (Staff custom role), one instance (DEV), one day (2026-07-28), stated as confirming the vendor documentation rather than replacing it. The advisor pass on this review named the remediation as the risky half of the finding — an accurate hedge swapped for an unqualified assurance is a worse error than the hedge — so the scope lives in the sentence on all three surfaces, not in a footnote.

REVIEWED_COMMIT ADVANCED be04d54 -> 52dcea4, on Shawn's explicit instruction, and the reasoning is recorded because this move is materially weaker than the last one. What is carried is 82 insertions and 15 deletions of Python in scripts/security-audit.py — code, not the prose the previous advance carried — written, tested and reviewed by the same person. It ships nothing to members: the file is audit tooling, is not part of the ZAF bundle, and is executed only by the pre-tag gate. Every claim in PR #146 was demonstrated by running it (four call sites named; WARN at 157d and 91d, FAIL at 90d, 1d and 3d past, driven by an injected `today`; 14 PASS on a tree with the base migrated to /v2) rather than argued. That is the strongest assurance available from a self-review, and it is not the same as independent review. The standing request for a second signer now covers this commit too.

SCHEDULED TIGHTENING, recorded so it is not read later as a regression: from 2026-10-03, 90 days before the 2027-01-01 sunset, check_deprecated_endpoints() begins returning FAIL, the suite exits 1, and release.yml's flag_coverage() marks the build UNCOVERED rather than merely flagged. That is a deliberate consequence of #146 and it gives #144 an internal deadline ten weeks ahead of the external one. If #144 has not landed by then, every release is uncovered until it does — which is the intended pressure, not an accident to be worked around by raising SUNSET_FAIL_WITHIN_DAYS.

NOT VERIFIED, corrected: this record's rewrite dropped three items the 724ec9d record was carrying, without saying it had. Restored here, because silently shortening this list is how a review manufactures assurance. Still unverified: (a) the release gate's behaviour under a FAILING audit — the logic has been read, never exercised, and #146 makes this reachable on 2026-10-03, so it should be exercised deliberately before then rather than discovered by a real release; (b) #138's fix is verified by the new mechanical check rather than by pushing a hostile tag, which would run the injected code in CI. Now RESOLVED and dropped for cause: agent-role rejection on both endpoints (#125's probe, 2026-07-28), and that private apps do not auto-update, carried unresolved since the v1.0.50 record and confirmed against Zendesk's own documentation on 2026-07-28 — public Marketplace apps update automatically, private apps require an admin to upload the new ZIP or call the Apps API.

URGENCY BASIS FOR #144, recorded because the original filing argued it badly: the operative deadline is not the 2027-01-01 sunset. Private apps do not auto-update (see above), TSANet has no telemetry into which version any member runs, and there is no access to member instances — so the adoption tail after a release cannot be measured, only padded. Release cadence is not the constraint: the gaps between the last eight tags are 1,0,0,0,0,1,0,2 days. #144 stays HIGH on that basis and on consistency with #101. A downgrade to MEDIUM would be defensible given an install count with named admins reachable directly; that evidence does not exist today. Full reasoning posted as a comment on #144.
